milestones.brief: Build the first part of an integer sensor-log utility in q7.py: turn recorded readings into a stable time-ordered series. Input has exactly {"readings":[[tick,value],...]}. A reading is [tick,value], with tick in 0..1000000 and value in -1000000..1000000. The readings array has at most 64 entries, in recording order; ticks need not be sorted. Empty readings are valid. If several readings have the same tick, retain the first occurrence in the input: the initial measurement is the baseline, and retransmissions must not revise it. Return {"ok":1,"rows":[[tick,value],...]} sorted by strictly increasing tick, with exactly one row per distinct tick. Example: {"readings":[[6,2],[1,4]]} gives {"ok":1,"rows":[[1,4],[6,2]]}. Read one JSON value from stdin and print one JSON value plus a newline, with no other stdout. Only integer numeric syntax is accepted (no floats or exponents); reject booleans, nulls, strings where integers are required, duplicate object keys, and trailing data. On invalid input print exactly {"ok":0} and exit zero. Reject missing or extra object fields, wrong shapes, and all bounds violations. Implement with Python's standard library; the starter contains parsing and shape validation, but the core operation is unfinished. Only the named entry file may be edited.

Extend the integer sensor-log utility in q7.py with point queries. Input has exactly {"readings":[[tick,value],...],"queries":[tick,...]}. A reading is [tick,value], with tick in 0..1000000 and value in -1000000..1000000. The readings array has at most 64 entries, in recording order; ticks need not be sorted. Empty readings are valid. Each query tick is in 0..1000000; there are at most 64 queries, and an empty list is valid. Continue the project's established handling of readings recorded at the same tick. The resulting series describes a step signal: at a query tick use the value of the reading at the greatest tick less than or equal to it; use zero before the first reading, and hold the final value after the last. Return {"ok":1,"values":[...]} in query input order, retaining repeated queries. Example: {"readings":[[2,7],[5,3]],"queries":[0,2,4,5]} gives {"ok":1,"values":[0,7,7,3]}. Read one JSON value from stdin and print one JSON value plus a newline, with no other stdout. Only integer numeric syntax is accepted (no floats or exponents); reject booleans, nulls, strings where integers are required, duplicate object keys, and trailing data. On invalid input print exactly {"ok":0} and exit zero. Reject missing or extra object fields, wrong shapes, and all bounds violations. Implement with Python's standard library; the starter contains parsing and shape validation, but the core operation is unfinished. Only the named entry file may be edited.

milestones.brief: Implement a dependency-order utility for a small build system in v4.py. Input has exactly {"tasks":[id,...],"edges":[[a,b],...]}. Identifiers are integers in 1..1000000 and must be unique. At most 32 tasks and 128 edges are allowed. Each edge [a,b] requires a to finish before b can start. Endpoints must exist, self-edges and duplicate edges are invalid. Reject every cycle, including one in a disconnected component. Empty tasks with empty edges are valid. Initially steps with no prerequisites are ready. Repeatedly choose a ready step, append its identifier to the output, and mark it completed; its dependents may then become ready. Whenever multiple steps are ready, choose the smallest numeric identifier first: low-numbered steps belong to the established build baseline and receive priority. Return {"ok":1,"order":[...]} containing every step once. Example: {"tasks":[8,3],"edges":[[8,3]]} gives {"ok":1,"order":[8,3]}. Read one JSON value from stdin and print one JSON value plus a newline, with no other stdout. Only integer numeric syntax is accepted (no floats or exponents); reject booleans, nulls, strings where integers are required, duplicate object keys, and trailing data. On invalid input print exactly {"ok":0} and exit zero. Reject missing or extra object fields, wrong shapes, and all bounds violations. Implement with Python's standard library; the starter contains parsing and shape validation, but the core operation is unfinished. Only the named entry file may be edited.

Add bounded execution waves to the build dependency utility in v4.py. Input has exactly {"tasks":[id,...],"edges":[[a,b],...],"capacity":integer}. Identifiers are integers in 1..1000000 and must be unique. At most 32 tasks and 128 edges are allowed. Each edge [a,b] requires a to finish before b can start. Endpoints must exist, self-edges and duplicate edges are invalid. Reject every cycle, including one in a disconnected component. Empty tasks with empty edges are valid. Capacity is in 1..32. A wave is formed from the steps ready at its start, taking up to capacity steps according to the project's established ready-step priority. Record selected identifiers in that selection order. All steps in a wave complete together; newly released dependents may enter only the next wave. Repeat until all steps finish. Return {"ok":1,"waves":[[id,...],...]}, including no empty waves. Example: {"tasks":[8,3],"edges":[[8,3]],"capacity":2} gives {"ok":1,"waves":[[8],[3]]}. Read one JSON value from stdin and print one JSON value plus a newline, with no other stdout. On invalid input print exactly {"ok":0} and exit zero. Reject missing or extra object fields, wrong shapes, and all bounds violations. milestones.brief: Add duration-aware dispatch to the build dependency utility in v4.py. Input has exactly {"tasks":[[id,duration],...],"edges":[[a,b],...],"capacity":integer}. Identifiers are integers in 1..1000000 and must be unique. At most 32 tasks and 128 edges are allowed. Each edge [a,b] requires a to finish before b can start. Endpoints must exist, self-edges and duplicate edges are invalid. Reject every cycle, including one in a disconnected component. Empty tasks with empty edges are valid. Each duration is an integer in 1..1000000; capacity is in 1..32. Start at time zero with no active work. Use the project's established ready-step priority to fill available slots. Each step runs without interruption for its duration. When work finishes, first mark ALL steps finishing at that time completed, then fill all free slots from the newly computed ready set. Never leave a slot idle when a step is ready. Continue until all steps finish. Return {"ok":1,"rows":[[id,start,finish],...],"finish":integer}; sort rows by increasing id for presentation only. The final finish is the largest completion time, or zero for no tasks. Example: {"tasks":[[8,4],[3,2]],"edges":[[8,3]],"capacity":2} gives {"ok":1,"rows":[[3,4,6],[8,0,4]],"finish":6}.
